body.statement: Let \(n\geq1\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, and let \(h:U\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous and injective. Then \(h(U)\) is open in \(\mathbb R^n\).

source.verbatim_statement: If U is an open set in R^n and h : U→R^n is a continuous injection, then the image h(U) is an open set in R^n.

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-11 against Allen Hatcher author-hosted Algebraic Topology PDF at https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf, Theorem 2B.3, printed p. 172 (PDF p. 180), lines 10769-10776 in the retrieved text.
